title: fanoutqa: Who were the heads of state of the belligerents in the War of the Third Coalition and when did they die? (114fef46b46c49e6)

chat_history.content: Who were the heads of state of the belligerents in the War of the Third Coalition and when did they die?

content.content:
The user asks: "Who were the heads of state of the belligerents in the War of the Third Coalition and when did they die?" Need to list the belligerents (countries) in the War of the Third Coalition (1805). The Third Coalition consisted of United Kingdom, Austria, Russia, Sweden, Naples (Kingdom of Naples), and perhaps others like Ottoman Empire (not directly?), also the Kingdom of Portugal? Let's recall: The Third Coalition (1805) was formed by Britain, Austria, Russia, Sweden, and Naples. Also maybe the Kingdom of Sardinia? Actually Sardinia joined later. The main belligerents: United Kingdom (King George III), Austrian Empire (Emperor Francis II), Russian Empire (Tsar Alexander I), Kingdom of Sweden (King Gustav IV Adolf), Kingdom of Naples (King Ferdinand IV, later Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies?). Also possibly the Ottoman Empire was neutral. Also the Republic of Venice was dissolved. So answer: heads of state and death dates.

We need to provide names and death dates.

List:

- United Kingdom: King George III (reigned 1760-1820). Died 29 January 1820.

- Austrian Empire: Francis II (Holy Roman Emperor Francis II, later Emperor Francis I of Austria). Died 21 March 1835.

- Russian Empire: Alexander I (Tsar). Died 1 December 1825.

- Sweden: Gustav IV Adolf (King). Died 13 February 1837.

- Kingdom of Naples (and later the Two Sicilies): Ferdinand IV of Naples (also Ferdinand III of Sicily) who became Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies. Died 4 January 1825.

Also possibly the Kingdom of Sardinia (Victor Emmanuel I) but they didn't join until 1805? Actually Sardinia joined the coalition after 1805? The Third Coalition included the Kingdom of Sardinia (Victor Emmanuel I) as part of the coalition? I think Sardinia was not part of the Third Coalition because it was occupied by French earlier. So not.

Also the Ottoman Empire not a belligerent.

Thus answer.

Will produce concise list with bullet points.

content:
**Heads of State of the Belligerent Powers in the War of the Third Coalition (1805) and Their Dates of Death**

| Belligerent (1805) | Head of State (title) | Lifespan (born – died) | Date of Death |
|--------------------|-----------------------|------------------------|---------------|
| **United Kingdom** | **King George III** (King of Great Britain & Ireland) | 4 June 1738 – 29 January 1820 | 29 January 1820 |
| **Austrian Empire** (also Holy Roman Emperor) | **Francis II** (Holy Roman Emperor) / **Francis I** (Emperor of Austria) | 12 February 1768 – 21 March 1835 | 21 March 1835 |
| **Russian Empire** | **Tsar Alexander I** | 23 December 1777 – 1 December 1825 | 1 December 1825 |
| **Kingdom of Sweden** | **King Gustav IV Adolf** | 1 November 1778 – 13 February 1837 | 13 February 1837 |
| **Kingdom of Naples (and Sicily)** | **King Ferdinand IV of Naples** (also **Ferdinand III of Sicily**, later **Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies**) | 12 January 1751 – 4 January 1825 | 4 January 1825 |

### Quick notes

- The **War of the Third Coalition** (1805) pitted Napoleon’s French Empire against the coalition of the United Kingdom, Austria, Russia, Sweden, and the Kingdom of Naples.  
- These were the **heads of state** of each belligerent at the time the war broke out (early‑1805).  
- All listed monarchs survived the war; their death dates range from 1820 (George III) to 1837 (Gustav IV Adolf).  

If you need additional details—such as the exact titles they held in 1805, their reign periods, or information on other participants (e.g., the Ottoman Empire, which remained neutral)—just let me know!
